examples.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-7x(t)+y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-7y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Find the general solution to the system of ODEs above.

*Hint: ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071035/assets/5388e1d5a2d29c3930b904d418b3a69615683bff1278d45a202d8405b150cede.png) where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071035/assets/85fc07cc4bce6e748a6b0184a3fc0a1ef75bf37e29d68ea45cbbb94892d5b58d.png)*
examples.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071035/assets/7f047425e15df4bb6bd8284f0e6267227ba31f6a251ceb45e040e6a508b519d6.png)
where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071035/assets/2dff913b6a0163c9dff6e28d81690472f043de69e4796dffb58b16b933165450.png) So, the matrix of the system is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071035/assets/c31b507ed2dac736cf47cbee9a967be4f4dc7deda44776e27a62be953834905b.png)

Given the system $\mathbf{x}'(t) = A \mathbf{x}(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as

$$
\mathbf{x}(t) = \Phi(t) \, \mathbf{c},
$$

where $\Phi(t)$ is a fundamental matrix of the system, and $\mathbf{c}$ is a constant vector.

Now, using the given information, the standard fundamental matrix $\Phi_0(t)$ of the system is given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071035/assets/716aafac0120d14538c3cb2cea689450e9655f0d94147b04c0903c3bb5cde753.png)

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={Φ}_{0}(t)\,c \\  & ={e}^{At}\,c \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-7t} & t{e}^{-7t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-7t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-7t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}t{e}^{-7t} \\ {e}^{-7t}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-7t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}t \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-7t},\end{aligned}
$$

where $c_1,c_2 \in \mathbb{R}.$
